name: Deaths in the Family
summary: Coleman Farthing, once a mill worker, seeks vengeance from Brill against the Agamand family. During the Third War, he stayed to defend their estate with his fellow workers, and they died beside their stubborn masters. The Agamands rose again as mindless thralls of the Lich King.

sections.title: A Legacy of Pride
sections.body: Before the Third War, the Agamands were Tirisfal Glades' wealthiest and most influential farming family. Their mills and fertile pastures yielded grain through the labor of dozens of tenant farmers and millers. When the Plague of Undeath crossed Lordaeron, the family refused to flee or abandon its ancestral lands. They believed their stone walls and loyal workers could hold back the horrors advancing from the east.

sections.title: The Price of Loyalty
sections.body: Coleman Farthing and the other workers trusted their lords' assurances and stayed to defend the estate. The Scourge overwhelmed them. The Agamands and their workers were slaughtered, then raised into undeath where they fell. Farthing eventually broke free through Sylvanas Windrunner's liberation. The Agamand patriarchs and heirs remained under the Lich King's mental grip, wandering the ruined mills as mindless Scourge sentries.

sections.title: Bitter Retribution
sections.body: Coleman Farthing now lives in Brill, still bitter toward the masters whose pride cost him his mortal life. Seeking vengeance and closure, he sends Forsaken champions to Agamand Mills to destroy Gregor, Nissa, and Thurman Agamand. He hopes his former masters kept enough awareness behind their rotting faces to feel terror as their unlife came to an end.

faq.answer: Before Lordaeron fell, the Agamands were Tirisfal Glades' wealthiest and most prosperous landowners. They owned and ran Agamand Mills, where they employed numerous local farmers and millers.

faq.q: Why is Coleman Farthing so angry at them?
aliases: why does farthing hate the agamands
faq.answer: Coleman Farthing worked at their mills. When the Scourge came, the Agamands persuaded their workers to stay and defend the estate instead of fleeing. Farthing blames their aristocratic pride for the deaths and undeath of him and his fellow workers.

faq.q: Did the Agamands join the Forsaken?
faq.answer: No. Coleman Farthing and other Forsaken broke free, but the Agamands remained under the Lich King's control. They still haunt the ruined family mills as mindless Scourge minions.

faq.q: Which Agamand family members must be destroyed?
faq.answer: You are sent to hunt Gregor Agamand, Nissa Agamand, and Thurman Agamand, then collect their remains from the family estate to confirm their destruction.
Agamand Mills lies in northern Tirisfal Glades, northwest of Brill. Ruined windmills and farmhouses fill the once-fertile estate, now infested with Scourge.

faq.q: What does Coleman Farthing do with their remains?
faq.answer: Coleman asks for their remains to confirm their destruction. They offer closure for his mortal grudges and proof that the lords who doomed him have been extinguished.

angles.text: As an Undead, you carry the personal grudges many Forsaken bear from mortal life. Lordaeron's fall left deep wounds and bitterness toward those who led them to ruin.
As a member of the Horde, you help remove dangerous Scourge commanders close to Brill and the Undercity's northern approaches.
